scope: Theorem 6.1 (Strong density bound in both orientations) of the manuscript “Routing densities and representation contraction for Thorp sweeps” (preprints/Routing-densities-and-representation-contraction-for-Thorp-sweeps-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4e5fbcff0dec65fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants p ∈ (1, 2] and C < ∞ such that, for every N = 2d, every coordinate order, every 0 ≤ l ≤ N, either choice of HN , and every x ∈ XN,l, 1 (N)l X y∈XN,l (N)lHN (x, y) p ≤ eCl . (20) After increasing C, the same constants give N−l X y∈{0,1}dl Nl HN (x, y) p ≤ eCl , (21) where the kernel is extended by zero on tuples with repeated positions. Both conclusions hold with rows replaced by columns.
